- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +1.5–2.0% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.3), model underestimates downward moves → add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon → if recent 7-day average is > 71.0, forecast should be capped at 71.5–72.0 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often fails to recognize momentum → add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast if last 3 days show > 2% drop.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly falling, model overestimates upside → reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts → if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead by -0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
